name: node-service
description: A Node.js/TypeScript API (for example Express, Fastify, Hono or NestJS), optionally with a built web frontend, often organised as an npm workspace.

runtimes.provision: <installed on dev and prod hosts; confirm the installed version actually matches what's declared>

build.command: npm run build  (in each workspace package that has one)

services.manager: <a service manager or a container runtime>
services.bind: <loopback-only, unless a trusted edge forwards identity>
services.health: <the app's real health route - confirm it, do not assume a default path>

routing.staticRoot: <built web frontend output folder, if any>

files: <the env file the API reads, per environment>
config.rule: kept out of version control; a committed example file with placeholder values

data.migrations: <the app's migration tool, if any, e.g. Prisma or Knex>

ci.workflow: <CI workflow file: lint (eslint), typecheck (tsc), test, build>

deploy.script: <deploy script: build in a staging copy, stop, swap, start>
verify: the health route returns a body with a status field, not just HTTP 200
a rendered page changed, so an old build behind a redeployed API cannot pass
